name: APIXTask
title: APIX Regulatory Task
description: Task profile for APIX regulatory submission workflows

constraint.human: A status reason is required when the status is rejected or cancelled.

element.short: Automatically updated on every change
Human-readable narrative

slicing.description: At least one mandatory technical UUID identifier. A regulator procedure number is optional.

element.short: Task instance UUID (required) + official regulator procedure number (optional), other identifiers allowed as well
Technical UUID for this specific Task instance

constraint.human: Identifier value must be a urn:uuid

element.short: Official regulator procedure/submission number (EMA, FDA, PMDA, etc.)
The actual regulator-assigned procedure number (format varies by authority)
Reference to the parent Task (e.g. a response points to the question Task), ordered lineage of Tasks (oldest → newest).
Parent/Set ID – groups all Tasks in the same regulatory procedure
Required if status is rejected or cancelled
element.definition: Required if status is rejected or cancelled. Reason for current status.

element.short: Detailed regulatory status (e.g., clock-stop)

binding.description: Detailed regulatory status such as clock-stop

element.short: Defines the regulatory message type and triggers specific business rules
element.definition: Defines the regulatory message type and triggers specific business rules

binding.description: Codes to identify what the task involves.  These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.

element.short: Identifies the medicinal product(s) that is the subject. For multiple products use Group or List FHIR Resource
element.definition: Identifies the medicinal product(s) that is the subject of the process, use Group or List FHIR Resource is there are multiple.

element.short: Requested period for task fulfilment
element.definition: The period during which the regulatory timeline (e.g., clock start to decision deadline) for the medicinal product procedure or response will be performed.

element.short: Clock-start / earliest allowed start
element.definition: The date/time when the regulatory clock starts or the earliest the task may begin.
element.comment: Example: Day 0 of a marketing-authorisation procedure, validation completion date, etc.

element.short: Deadline / clock-stop date
element.definition: The latest date/time by which the task must be completed.
element.comment: Example: Day 210 of centralised procedure, response deadline to List of Questions, etc.

element.short: Actual execution period
element.definition: The actual time period during which the task was performed (e.g., when validation actually started and when it was completed).

element.short: Actual start time
Actual completion time
Date/time the sender created the Task
element.definition: Starting point for regulatory cycle-time metrics.

element.short: Organization that initiated the task
element.definition: The person or system that **created** the Task and wants the work done. In regulatory context: The Regulatory Authority (e.g., FDA/EMA) or a senior manager initiating a submission review.

element.short: The Organization accountable for fulfilling the Task.
element.definition: The organization, person or system currently **responsible** for fulfillng the Task.

element.short: Organization or individual who performed the task
element.definition: Organization or individual who performed the task. Can be different from the Task.owner.

element.short: Input parameters for the task
element.definition: Additional information that may be needed for fulfilment of the task in the context of medicinal product regulatory procedures.

element.short: Input type  indicates the type of input, such as the code used as a DocumentReference type

binding.description: Codes to identify types of input parameters.  These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.  E.g. "Comparison source", "Applicable consent", "Concomitent Medications", etc.

element.short: Output produced by the task
element.definition: Outputs produced by the task in the context of medicinal product regulatory procedures.

element.short: Output type indicates the type of output, such as the code used as a DocumentReference type

binding.description: Codes to identify types of input parameters.  These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.  E.g. "Identified issues", "Preliminary results", "Filler order", "Final results", etc.
